content.title: About
content.content: KIND Fruit and Nut Bar is a whole‑food snack bar made with dried fruit, nuts, seeds, and whole grains. It contains no artificial flavors, colors, or gluten and is marketed as a healthy, vegetarian-friendly snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Each bar contains at least five different nuts and dried fruits.
KIND uses only whole ingredients and no hydrogenated oils.
The bar is certified vegan and gluten‑free.
It provides roughly 12 g of protein per serving thanks to nuts and seeds.
KIND supports food‑waste reduction initiatives and uses recyclable packaging.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Dried fruit and whole grains supply dietary fiber that supports normal digestion.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: Nuts and seeds provide monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: The bar contains vitamin E, magnesium, and potassium, which aid nerve and muscle function.

items.title: Low added sugar
items.content: Sweetness comes from natural fruit sugars without refined sugar added.

items.title: Satiety support
items.content: The combination of protein, fat, and fiber helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: The bar contains nuts (almond, cashew, hazelnut) that may trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: One bar provides about 200 kcal, so portion control is advisable within a daily diet.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Although the sugar is natural, individuals with diabetes should monitor their intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The bar is convenient as an on‑the‑go snack between meals, can be chopped into yogurt or oatmeal, or used as an energy boost before workouts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in its original packaging. After opening, reseal the bag and consume within 7‑10 days.

content.title: About
content.content: Steamed haddock is a tender white fish with a mild flavor and low fat content. Steaming preserves most of its nutrients, keeping the flesh moist and easy to digest.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Haddock is one of the most widely caught marine fish, harvested in the North Atlantic and Pacific oceans.
Steaming retains up to 90 % of B‑vitamins, which are easily destroyed by frying.
The meat is low in calories—about 85 kcal per 100 g—yet high in protein.
Haddock is a staple in traditional Northern European dishes, often prepared in a steamed version of fish‑and‑chips.
Unlike many other fish, haddock contains virtually no mercury.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: A 100‑g serving of steamed haddock provides roughly 18 g of high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Haddock contains less than 1 g of fat per 100 g, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Steamed haddock supplies vitamin B12, niacin, and vitamin B6, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It is a good source of selenium, phosphorus, and iodine, important for thyroid health and immunity.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: While lower than in fatty fish, steamed haddock still provides EPA and DHA omega‑3s.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to fish, including haddock.

items.title: Contamination
items.content: Although mercury levels are low, purchase fish from reputable sources to avoid other contaminants.

items.title: Digestive sensitivity
items.content: Large portions may cause discomfort for people with a sensitive stomach.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve steamed haddock with lemon, fresh herbs (dill, parsley) and a light yogurt‑based sauce. It pairs well with boiled potatoes, quinoa, or vegetable sides.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh haddock in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C for up to 2 days. Frozen fish should be stored at –18 °C for up to 3 months. Rinse and pat dry before cooking.

content.title: About
content.content: Fruit cocktail, canned (NFS) is a mixture of diced fruits in a sweet syrup, packaged in glass or metal cans. The product follows the NFS (No Further Specification) standard, meaning no extra additives beyond sugar and a preservative. Typical fruits include pineapple, peach, pear, orange and cherry.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canning preserves fruit flavor and nutrients for up to 2‑3 years.
The syrup often contains a small amount of citric acid to stabilize fruit colour.
Fruit canning became popular in the 19th century and spread worldwide.
Fruit cocktail is frequently used in desserts, salads, and as a topping for yogurt.
In many countries it is also called "fruit mix" or "fruit salad in a jar".

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: The fruits provide vitamin C, which supports the immune system and aids iron absorption.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Diced fruits contain soluble and insoluble fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports heart function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Canned fruit cocktail contains virtually no fat, making it a light snack.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Fruit polyphenols and carotenoids have antioxidant properties that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The syrup usually contains a high amount of sugar, which may be problematic for people with diabetes or those watching their weight.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Preservatives such as potassium sorbate may be used, which can cause sensitivity in some individuals.

items.title: Fruit allergy
items.content: People allergic to specific fruits (e.g., pineapple or peach) should avoid the product.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The acidic syrup can irritate the stomach in persons with high gastric acidity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fruit cocktail can be eaten straight from the jar, added to oatmeal, yogurt, cottage cheese, used in baking, or as a filling for pancakes and crepes. If you want to reduce sugar, lightly drain the syrup before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 5‑7 days. Discard if you notice mold, off‑smell, or any change in texture.

content.title: About
content.content: A hamburger bun made from wheat or cracked wheat flour is soft, slightly sweet, and airy. It serves as a convenient base for burgers, holding meat, vegetables, and sauces without falling apart when heated.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditionally these buns are made with wheat flour, but some recipes incorporate cracked wheat for a denser texture.
In the United States they are commonly sold in packs of 8–12, while in Russia they are found in bakeries and supermarkets.
Sesame‑topped buns are popular, adding extra aroma and crunch.
Buns can be fresh or frozen; frozen buns retain flavor and structure after baking.
Some versions include a small amount of sugar and milk to improve crust color and softness.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: The bun provides a quick source of energy through easily digestible carbs.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: When whole‑grain or cracked wheat flour is used, the bun supplies fiber that supports digestion.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Wheat flour contains thiamine, niacin, and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Iron, magnesium, and phosphorus are present, contributing to normal body functions.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Traditional recipes are low in fat, making the bun a suitable component of a balanced diet.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Wheat buns contain gluten, which can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Rapidly absorbed carbs may raise blood sugar levels, so portion control is advised for diabetics.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some recipes add salt; excessive sodium intake can affect blood pressure.

items.title: Preservatives in commercial versions
items.content: Store‑bought buns may contain additives and preservatives that are not suitable for everyone.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the bun horizontally, lightly toast it on a grill or toaster, then add the patty, cheese, vegetables, and sauces. It can also be used for sandwiches, as a base for appetizers, or served alongside soup.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep buns in a cool, dry place in a paper bag or sealed container for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze them in an airtight bag – they retain quality for up to 2 months. Warm in the oven or toaster before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: Rice soup is a traditional dish popular in many cuisines. The basic ingredients are boiled rice and broth (meat, chicken or vegetable). The dish has a mild flavor, light texture and can be enriched with vegetables, spices and herbs.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Rice soup is often served in cold weather as a warming meal.
In Japan there is a version called "okayu" where rice is cooked directly in the broth, creating a thick consistency.
In some regions of Russia rice soup is considered a "recovery food" after illness.
Rice absorbs some of the broth’s nutrients, making the dish more balanced.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Rice provides slowly digestible carbs that give a lasting feeling of fullness.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Warm broth and soft rice are gentle on the stomach, useful for digestive issues.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Rice contains thiamine, niacin and vitamin B6, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Rice supplies magnesium, phosphorus and iron, supporting muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The broth component helps maintain the body’s water balance.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared broth can be high in salt; people with hypertension should monitor sodium intake.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: The soup may contain vegetables, spices or meat that can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Adding large amounts of oil or cream can make the soup calorie‑rich.

items.title: Contamination during storage
items.content: Leftover soup should be cooled quickly and stored in the refrigerator to prevent bacterial growth.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve rice soup hot, often garnished with fresh herbs, lemon wedges or green onions. You can add boiled vegetables, chicken, seafood or tofu to vary flavor and nutritional value.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For freezing, transfer to freezer‑safe bags and use within 2‑3 months. Reheat to a rolling boil before serving.

stuffed-shells-cheese-filled-with-tomato.title: Stuffed shells, cheese-filled, with tomato sauce, meatless

content.title: About
content.content: Stuffed shells are large pasta shells filled with creamy cheese, sometimes seasoned with herbs and spices, and baked in a tomato sauce. This vegetarian dish contains no meat but provides protein from the cheese and carbohydrates from the pasta.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditionally, stuffed shells are an Italian specialty known as "conchiglioni".
The creamy cheese filling keeps the shells tender and helps them hold their shape during baking.
The tomato sauce is often made from ripe tomatoes, basil, and olive oil, giving the dish a bright aroma.
The recipe can be easily adapted for various diets by adding spinach, mushrooms, or vegan cheese.
Stuffed shells are popular in festive menus because they look impressive and are easy to portion.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Cream cheese is a good source of calcium, which supports bone and tooth health.

items.title: Provides protein
items.content: The cheese filling supplies plant‑based protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: Lycopene in tomato sauce
items.content: Tomatoes contain lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Using low‑fat cheese makes the dish contain less saturated fat than meat‑based versions.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Cheese and whole‑grain pasta provide B1, B2, and B12 vitamins important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cream cheese contains lactose; people with intolerance should choose lactose‑free alternatives.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to cheese.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Cheeses can be salty; those with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Pasta glycemic index
items.content: Regular pasta has a high glycemic index; whole‑grain or legume‑based pasta can lower the impact.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot, garnished with fresh basil or parsley. Sprinkle grated Parmesan or vegan cheese on top if desired. The dish is eaten with a fork and knife and works well as individual portions on a plate.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked stuffed shells in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For freezing, place in a freezer‑safe bag and use within 2 months. Reheat until the sauce is bubbling.

content.title: About
content.content: Toddler meal, rice and vegetables is a ready‑to‑serve dish designed for children aged 12 months and older. It contains boiled rice, gently steamed vegetables (carrot, broccoli, cauliflower) and a small amount of vegetable oil. The meal is balanced in protein, carbohydrates and fats, easy to digest and suitable for daily nutrition.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Rice is one of the most hypoallergenic grains and is widely used in baby foods.
Vegetables are steamed to retain maximum vitamins and minerals.
Dietary fiber from the vegetables supports healthy bowel function in toddlers.
The product contains no added sugar, salt or artificial flavors.
Each serving provides about 200‑250 kcal, matching the daily energy needs of a 12‑24‑month‑old child.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Rice supplies a steady release of energy, keeping the child active throughout the day.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B3 and B6 support normal nervous system development and metabolism.

items.title: Vitamin A and carotenoids
items.content: Carrot and broccoli provide provitamin A, essential for vision and immune function.

items.title: Calcium and magnesium
items.content: The small amount of oil and vegetables delivers minerals needed for bone and teeth growth.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Helps establish a healthy gut microbiome and prevents constipation.

items.title: Rice allergy
items.content: Although rare, some children may develop an allergic reaction to rice.

items.title: Over‑consumption
items.content: Large portions can contribute to excess calorie intake and unwanted weight gain.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The product contains no added salt, but when combined with other foods, total sodium should be monitored.

items.title: Texture for young toddlers
items.content: For children under 12 months, larger vegetable pieces may pose a choking hazard; puree if needed.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Warm the portion to body temperature, stir until smooth. If a softer texture is needed, add a little breast milk or infant formula. Serve in a clean baby bowl without extra salt, sugar or sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the package in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, use within 3‑5 days and store in the refrigerator at 2‑4 °C. Discard if you notice off‑odors or discoloration.
